title: Joe Keyes's playing and the 'out of tune' review
summary: Keyes was a good swinging lead trumpet on a poor horn; George Simon's Metronome review said the band was out of tune.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Now what about Joe Keyes? Jo Jones has spoken very highly to me about him as a musician.
He was a very good musician. Very good trumpet player. But he always played a bad horn. He never did have a good trumpet. He always played a little bit out of tune.
I don't know. I know we got a terrible write-up in (George Simon?).*
You know about the write up he did?
He said, if you don't believe the saxophones is out of tune, just listen to the trumpets. He said, if you don't believe the trumpets is out of tune, just listen to the whole band.
Well, Basie read that the next day and got mad. And he still talks about it. But I told George Simon way later, I said, you know, I think I know you're right, but we were, we weren't (in tune?)

But they weren't concentrating on being in tune, they were concentrating on swinging. And Joe Keyes was a good swinging first trumpet player except for that. If he had a good horn it might have been a different thing. But he had a horn that had rubbers all around it.
He'd keep this valve from sliding out with a piece of string on it to hold it in place.
